tier_rationale: Manufacturer specifications list no connectivity, ports, wireless or data transfer of any kind, and the calculator is approved for the SAT, ACT and AP exams — approvals that exclude any device with communication capability.
the_unplug_test: It does arithmetic. There is no port, no radio, no cable, and no firmware to update. A solar cell assists the battery, so for most of its life it does not even need that replaced. This is a device whose behaviour on the day you buy it is the behaviour it will have forever.

repairability.notes: Hard plastic body with a snap-on cover and a user-replaceable cell assisted by a solar panel. Nothing to service beyond the battery.

sources.supports: Manufacturer specifications list no USB port, wireless capability or data transfer option. Battery powered with solar assistance. Stated as approved for SAT, ACT and AP exams — approvals that categorically exclude devices with communication capability.
Manufacturer guidebook documents operation entirely through the keypad, with no pairing, linking, or computer-connection procedure anywhere in the manual.

notes: Included partly to record the exam-approval heuristic, which generalises well beyond calculators: standardised-testing bodies prohibit any device capable of communication, so an SAT/ACT/AP approval is a third party with enforcement power certifying the absence of a radio. Note that TI's graphing calculators do have link ports and USB, so the approval attaches to this model rather than to the brand.
